title: Systems Ethology Platform
text:
← Back to Demos Gallery
The Systems Ethology Platform (ewingApp()) serves as the central interactive hub for the ewing simulation package. Based on inst/shinyApp/app.R, it integrates species parameter initialization, event-driven competing risk transitions, substrate interactions, temperature regime Splines, and multi-run confidence envelope estimations.

title: Systems Ethology Platform
text:
Interactive Application Usage
You can launch the full Systems Ethology interactive application natively in R:
library(ewing)

# Launch central Shiny app
ewingApp()

[!NOTE] Live Deployment: The full interactive Systems Ethology application is deployed live on Posit Connect (SystemsEthology).

title: Systems Ethology Platform
text:
Platform Components & Architecture
The platform combines modular Shiny components (ewingInput, ewingOutput, ewingServer) defined in R/ewingApp.R and deployed via inst/shinyApp/app.R:

Parameter Initialization (initParApp): Configure species life stage durations, attack rates, and reproduction probabilities.
Simulation Engine (simApp): Execute competing-risk event queues on leftist tree structures.
Dynamic Visualizations (distPlotApp, substrateApp, envPlotApp): Monitor real-time stage distributions, spatial agent positions, and multi-run variance envelopes.
Spatial & Hexagonal Integration (hexmapApp): Project abstract substrate coordinates onto real-world USGS watershed geography.

title: hexmoveApp (Organism Movement on Hex Grid)
text:
← Back to Demos Gallery
The hexmoveApp() application visualizes host and parasite spatial positions mapped directly onto a unified hexagonal substrate network topology (create_substrate).
Instead of rendering substrate components (fr1..fr4, tw1..tw2, lftop, lfbot) in isolated rectangular panel facets, hexmoveApp() places every organism on a continuous hexagonal substrate plane based on its native tridiagonal coordinates \((a, b, c)\) rescaled into its active substrate patch area.

title: hexmoveApp (Organism Movement on Hex Grid)
text:
Interactive Application Usage
Launch the application natively in R:
library(ewing)

# Initialize simulation and run initial 100 steps
mysim <- init.simulation()
mysim <- future.events(mysim, nstep = 100)

# Launch interactive Shiny app
hexmoveApp(mysim)

[!NOTE] Live Deployment: You can also test hexmoveApp() live on the SystemsEthology Connect Platform.

title: hexmoveApp (Organism Movement on Hex Grid)
text:
Key Features

Per-Substrate Unit Triangle Rescaling: Organisms’ local tridiagonal coordinates \((pos.a, pos.b, pos.c)\) are normalized and scaled into the unit triangle \([0, W_{sub}]\) of each active substrate patch, guaranteeing all individuals sit strictly within their substrate bounds (and supporting substrates of varying sizes).
Hexagonal Polygon Overlay: Generates discrete 6-sided polygon cells (create_hex_overlay) across all plant substrate components (fr1..fr4, tw1, lftop, lfbot).
Interactive Simulation Stepping: Action buttons (Step +1, Step +10, Step +100, Reset) allow stepping through simulation horizon events with live reactive map updates.
Modular Layout Composition: Seamlessly switch between "hex" (global hexagonal grid overlay) and "facet" (panel view faceted by substrate element) layouts in substrateInput / substrateServer.

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
← Back to Demos Gallery
The hexmapApp() application provides an interactive interface for discovering USGS subwatersheds, isolating specific geographic features (such as island landmasses), and projecting spatial hexagonal substrate networks for quantitative population ethology simulations.

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
Interactive Application Usage
You can launch the interactive application natively in R:
library(ewing)

# Launch interactive Shiny app
hexmapApp()

[!NOTE] Live Deployment: The interactive application requires dynamic spatial intersection libraries (sf) and live USGS / OpenStreetMap API access. It is deployed live on Posit Connect (HexMap).

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
section: Workflow Example: Isle Royale Watershed Projection
text:
Workflow Example: Isle Royale Watershed Projection
Below is an example showing how get_watershed() retrieves the USGS HUC12 subwatershed boundary (041800000101), clips it to the Isle Royale landmass using OpenStreetMap nominatim geometry (when osmdata is available), and overlays a spatial hexagonal grid (add_watershed_hex_overlay).

library(ewing)
library(ggplot2)

# Check if osmdata is installed for feature boundary restriction
feat_name <- if (requireNamespace("osmdata", quietly = TRUE)) "Isle Royale" else NULL

# 1. Fetch HUC12 boundary (optionally restricted to Isle Royale island landmass)
huc_info <- get_watershed("041800000101", feature_name = feat_name)

# 2. Construct spatial hexagonal overlay mesh (diameter = 0.01 degrees)
hex_obj <- add_watershed_hex_overlay(huc_info, hex_diameter = 0.01)

# 3. Visualize using autoplot
ggplot2::autoplot(hex_obj)

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
Technical Features

Leaflet Spatial Discovery: Click any location on North America or search landmark strings to reverse-geocode coordinates into USGS HUC12 subwatershed IDs (get_huc_from_point).
Feature Isolation: Clip large HUC boundaries covering open water to target landmasses (e.g. Isle Royale) using osmdata::getbb().
Hexagonal Mesh Scaling: Parameterize cell extent diameter to scale spatial resolution dynamically.
